headline: PM Kills Littering to keep Bangladesh clean and litter-free
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman urges citizens to be more responsible for environmental protection and creating a livable Bangladesh.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called upon citizens to be more responsible in protecting the environment to build a clean and livable Bangladesh.
In a message shared on his verified Facebook page on Monday (August 3), the Prime Minister emphasized that every citizen has a crucial role to play alongside the state in maintaining cleanliness.
He stated that if everyone fulfills their responsibilities properly, the country can achieve a clean environment and a beautiful nation.
The Prime Minister urged the public to be conscious of keeping their surroundings clean, noting that the country belongs to everyone.
He highlighted that small initiatives and collective efforts can bring about significant changes for the country.
The appeal has already received widespread response on social media, focusing on increasing awareness and active citizen participation.

headline_marked: 4.7 lakh children [[vaccinated in special drive]] to curb measles outbreak
headline: 4.7 lakh children vaccinated in special drive to curb measles outbreak
summary: A week-long 'mop-up' campaign successfully reached thousands of previously unvaccinated children after the government admitted targeting errors in the initial drive.
details: A special week-long 'mop-up' drive vaccinated 4,74,567 children aged six to 59 months against measles and rubella between July 26 and August 1.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), this effort averaged about 67,795 vaccinations per day, a massive increase over previous months.
The drive followed government admission that the initial nationwide emergency campaign's targets were inaccurate, leaving many children unprotected.
Public health experts had criticized the gap in coverage, which contributed to a severe outbreak with over 1,000 cases and 900 hospitalisations reported daily in July.
The crisis peaked on July 27, when Bangladesh recorded its highest daily measles hospitalisation of 1,415 patients.
Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hussain ordered the mop-up drive to ensure all eligible children are identified and vaccinated, including through home visits.
DGHS officials stated that the campaign will continue until every household has been covered to stop the spread of the virus.
caption:
4.7 lakh children were vaccinated in just one week. Why was this emergency 'mop-up' drive necessary?

A special week-long 'mop-up' drive vaccinated 4,74,567 children aged six to 59 months against measles and rubella between July 26 and August 1.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), this effort averaged about 67,795 vaccinations per day, a massive increase over previous months.

The drive followed government admission that the initial nationwide emergency campaign's targets were inaccurate, leaving many children unprotected.

Public health experts had criticized the gap in coverage, which contributed to a severe outbreak with over 1,000 cases and 900 hospitalisations reported daily in July.

The crisis peaked on July 27, when Bangladesh recorded its highest daily measles hospitalisation of 1,415 patients.

Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hussain ordered the mop-up drive to ensure all eligible children are identified and vaccinated, including through home visits.

DGHS officials stated that the campaign will continue until every household has been covered to stop the spread of the virus.
